question: How should ecommerce founders use AI interviews to develop better project plans?
transcript_excerpt: Instead of specifying exactly what you want AI to do step-by-step, start with an interview format where you give AI your general concept and let it ask clarifying questions one at a time. This allows AI to formulate its own plan based on your desires and context, discover capabilities you might not know about, and adapt follow-up questions based on your answers rather than asking redundant questions all at once.

question: What is the AI interview technique for content creators managing multiple video variations?
transcript_excerpt: When you have multiple content angles like three hooks, two bodies, and two CTAs creating 12 possible combinations, each requiring different overlays, captions, animations, and audio, you can use AI to help manage this complexity. Josh uses this technique as a content creator who produces 10 to 12 video variations weekly with different visual hooks, text overlays, and sound effects for testing different messaging angles.

question: Why is asking AI one question at a time better than multiple-choice prompts?
transcript_excerpt: When AI asks multiple questions at once in a dialogue format, users often select 'other' and type out thoughtful responses, then the next question asks something already covered. Asking one question at a time lets AI adapt its next questions based on your specific answers, change its line of questioning when you provide new information, and avoid redundancy—for example, if you mention wanting a report sent to your assistant, it will reframe subsequent questions around that new requirement.

question: How can content creators use AI to convert static creative testing into video production?
transcript_excerpt: Dylan's approach is to test messaging with static creatives first to identify what works, then go deeper with video as a modality. They test static creatives for messaging, find the winners, and then develop video variations around proven angles rather than going straight to video production, which makes more efficient use of production resources.
